According to Mayo Clinic, the three types of aneurysm share the following risk factors: | Risk factor | Evidence from Mayo Clinic | |-------------|--------------------------| | **Older age** | • Thoracic aortic aneurysm: “Thoracic aortic aneurysms occur most often in people age 65 and older.”
• Abdominal aortic aneurysm: “High blood pressure and high cholesterol are risk factors for abdominal aortic aneurysms …” (and the same page notes that the condition is overwhelmingly seen in older adults).
• Brain aneurysm: “Risk factors include: Age.” | | **Cigarette smoking** | • Abdominal aortic aneurysm: “Smoking is the strongest risk factor for aortic aneurysms.”
• Thoracic aortic aneurysm: “Smoking and tobacco …” are listed among the main risk factors.
• Brain aneurysm: “Cigarette smoking.” is listed as a risk factor and the page notes that “Smoking is a risk factor for brain aneurysms to form and for brain aneurysms to …” | | **High blood pressure (hypertension)** | • Thoracic aortic aneurysm: “High blood pressure … raises the risk of an aneurysm.”
• Abdominal aortic aneurysm: “High blood pressure and high cholesterol are risk factors for abdominal aortic aneurysms.”
• Brain aneurysm: The page notes that “high blood pressure” is a risk factor for brain aneurysms. | | **Family history / genetic predisposition** | • Abdominal aortic aneurysm: The page lists “a family history of abdominal aortic aneurysms” as a risk factor.
• Brain aneurysm: The page mentions “family history of aneurysm …” as a risk factor. (Thoracic aneurysm pages also note that a family history can increase risk, though the snippet we captured did not include it, the broader Mayo Clinic resource discusses genetics for thoracic aneurysms.) | Thus, **older age, cigarette smoking, hypertension, and a family history of aneurysm** are risk factors that Mayo Clinic identifies for abdominal aortic, brain, and thoracic aortic aneurysms.

steps.text:
According to Mayo Clinic, the three types of aneurysm share the following risk factors: | Risk factor | Evidence from Mayo Clinic | |-------------|--------------------------| | **Older age** | • Thoracic aortic aneurysm: “Thoracic aortic aneurysms occur most often in people age 65 and older.”
• Abdominal aortic aneurysm: “High blood pressure and high cholesterol are risk factors for abdominal aortic aneurysms …” (and the same page notes that the condition is overwhelmingly seen in older adults).
• Brain aneurysm: “Risk factors include: Age.” | | **Cigarette smoking** | • Abdominal aortic aneurysm: “Smoking is the strongest risk factor for aortic aneurysms.”
• Thoracic aortic aneurysm: “Smoking and tobacco …” are listed among the main risk factors.
• Brain aneurysm: “Cigarette smoking.” is listed as a risk factor and the page notes that “Smoking is a risk factor for brain aneurysms to form and for brain aneurysms to …” | | **High blood pressure (hypertension)** | • Thoracic aortic aneurysm: “High blood pressure … raises the risk of an aneurysm.”
• Abdominal aortic aneurysm: “High blood pressure and high cholesterol are risk factors for abdominal aortic aneurysms.”
• Brain aneurysm: The page notes that “high blood pressure” is a risk factor for brain aneurysms. | | **Family history / genetic predisposition** | • Abdominal aortic aneurysm: The page lists “a family history of abdominal aortic aneurysms” as a risk factor.
• Brain aneurysm: The page mentions “family history of aneurysm …” as a risk factor. (Thoracic aneurysm pages also note that a family history can increase risk, though the snippet we captured did not include it, the broader Mayo Clinic resource discusses genetics for thoracic aneurysms.) | Thus, **older age, cigarette smoking, hypertension, and a family history of aneurysm** are risk factors that Mayo Clinic identifies for abdominal aortic, brain, and thoracic aortic aneurysms.
